The graph of the function $f(x)$ is shown above. 
Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=5$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h},
$$

at the point $x=5$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(5) & ≈\frac{f(5+1)-f(5-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{f(6)-f(4)}{2} \\  & =\frac{5-2}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The population growth of a developing rural area was studied for $25$ years. The following table shows the population $p(t),$ in hundreds, recorded $t$ years after $1990.$

| **$t$** | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ | $25$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $p(t)$ | $90$ | $98$ | $116$ | $138$ | $178$ | $220$ |

$$

$$

Approximate the population growth rate in the year $2005$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=5.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{p}^{′}(x)≈\frac{p(t+h)-p(t-h)}{2h}.
$$

 
We note that year $2005$ corresponds to $t=15.$ The step size is $h=5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(15) & ≈\frac{p(15+5)-p(15-5)}{2(5)} \\  & =\frac{p(20)-p(10)}{2(5)} \\  & =\frac{178-116}{10} \\  & =\frac{62}{10} \\  & =6.2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the population growth rate in $2005$ was $620$ people per year.

questions.problem:
In a physics experiment, the net charge on a sensor (in $mC$) after $t$ seconds is given by the function $Q(t).$ The values of $Q(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $1.0$ | $1.5$ | $2.0$ | $2.5$ | $3.0$ | $3.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$Q(t)$** | $4$ | $3$ | $2$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-2$ |

Approximate the sensor’s charge instantaneous rate of change at $t=2.5$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=0.5.$

The sensor’s charge at $t=2.5$ is decreasing at approximately 
{{field-1}} $mC$ per second.
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{Q}^{′}(t)≈\frac{Q(t+h)-Q(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at time $t=2.5$ with step size $h=0.5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}^{′}(2.5) & ≈\frac{Q(2.5+0.5)-Q(2.5-0.5)}{2(0.5)} \\  & =\frac{Q(3.0)-Q(2.0)}{1.0} \\  & =\frac{-1-2}{1.0} \\  & =\frac{-3}{1.0} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sensor’s charge at $t=2.5$ is decreasing at approximately $3\,mC$ per second.
